layers.name: Gwangalli night walk: Gwangan Stn → beach → Millak raw-fish town → Millak Waterfront Park, 2.9 km (광안리 야간 산책)

line.name: Gwangalli night walk: Gwangan Station exit 3 → Gwangalli Beach → Millak fish market → Millak Waterfront Park under the bridge (광안역 → 광안리해수욕장 → 민락수변공원), 2.9 km

segments.label: Gwangan Station exit 3 down Gwangan-ro to the beach road (pedestrian router on OSM streets)
East along the beach road and the Galmaet-gil promenade to the Millak end
Through the Millak raw-fish town to the waterfront park under the bridge

pins.name: Start – Gwangan Station exit 3 (광안역(박원욱병원)3번출구)
pins.desc: Busan Metro line 2. Walk straight down Gwangan-ro for 10 minutes; the bridge appears at the end of the street.

pins.name: Gwangalli Beach (광안리해수욕장)
pins.desc: 1.4 km of sand facing Gwangan Bridge, lit in changing colours after dark. Walk the promenade east with the bridge ahead of you; the bar and café strip runs behind the beach road.

pins.name: Gwangan Bridge, the Diamond Bridge (광안대교(다이아몬드브릿지))
pins.desc: 7.4 km double-deck bridge across Suyeong Bay, Busan's night-time symbol. The light show changes by season and runs on the hour after dark.

pins.name: Gwangalli café street (광안리카페거리)
pins.desc: The lanes one block behind the beach: rooftop and upper-floor cafés with the bridge in the window.

pins.name: Millak raw-fish town (민락회타운)
pins.desc: Blocks of raw-fish restaurants at the east end of the beach; the cheaper way is the fish market next door.

pins.name: Millak fishermen's live-fish market (민락어민활어직판장)
pins.desc: Buy the fish downstairs by weight, carry it upstairs and pay a per-person setting fee for the table, side dishes and soup; or take it to the park outside. The most Busan dinner there is.

pins.name: End – Millak Waterfront Park (민락수변공원)
pins.desc: Steps and lawns right under the bridge, where locals sit on mats with sashimi and beer; the best spot for the Saturday drone show. Toilets at the park.

pins.name: Millak Port (민락항)
pins.desc: Small fishing harbour beyond the park; the coast road continues to Haeundae from here.

pins.name: Jagalchi Market (부산자갈치시장)
pins.desc: Korea's biggest fish market: tanks and stalls on the ground floor, restaurants that cook your pick upstairs, and the open-air quay stalls outside. Jagalchi Station exit 10.

pins.name: BIFF Square (비프광장)
pins.desc: Where the Busan film festival began: handprints in the pavement, cinemas, street-food carts and the famous ssiat hotteok queue.

pins.name: Gukje Market (국제시장)
pins.desc: The post-war goods market: arcades of clothes, kitchenware and street food, five minutes from Jagalchi.

pins.name: Bupyeong Kkangtong Market (부평깡통시장)
pins.desc: 'Tin-can market' next to Gukje, with the night food alley from early evening.

pins.name: Busan Tower, Yongdusan Park (부산타워)
pins.desc: Escalators from Gwangbok-ro up to the park and the 120 m tower; the city and port view at dusk.

pins.name: Jagalchi Station (자갈치역 부산1호선)
pins.desc: Line 1; exit 10 for the market, exit 7 for BIFF Square.

pins.name: Yeongdo Bridge (영도대교)
pins.desc: The 1934 bascule bridge to Yeongdo, raised at 14:00 daily; cross it on foot for Huinnyeoul.

pins.name: Huinnyeoul Culture Village (흰여울문화마을)
pins.desc: White houses on the Yeongdo cliff above the sea, a film set turned café lane. Quieter than Gamcheon with the same kind of photos. Bus 7, 71 or 508 from Nampo-dong.

pins.name: Huinnyeoul coastal tunnel (흰여울 해안터널)
pins.desc: Short tunnel through the rock from the village lane down to the Jeoryeong coast walk.

pins.name: Gamcheon Culture Village (감천문화마을)
pins.desc: Pastel houses stacked down the hillside, built by Taegeukdo refugees after the Korean War. Bus 1-1, 2 or 2-2 from Toseong Station; buy the stamp map at the information centre.

pins.name: Gamcheon Culture Village information centre (감천문화마을안내센터)
pins.desc: Stamp map, lockers and toilets at the village entrance.

pins.name: The Little Prince and the fox (감천문화마을어린왕자)
pins.desc: The most queued photo in Busan: the statue on the railing with the whole village behind. Weekday mornings have the shortest line.

pins.name: Toseong Station exit 6 (토성역6번출구)
pins.desc: Line 1; the village buses leave from the stop in front of the hospital.

pins.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple (해동용궁사)
pins.desc: The temple on the rocks above the sea, one of very few in Korea by the water: 108 steps down, the dragon and Buddha statues, sunrise crowds on New Year. Bus 181 from Haeundae Station, about 40 minutes.

pins.name: Haedong Yonggungsa car park and bus stop (해동용궁사주차장)
pins.desc: Where the bus drops you; the food stalls and toilets are along the lane down to the temple gate.

pins.name: Toilet – Gwangalli Beach (광안리해수욕장)
pins.desc: Public toilets along the beach promenade, west and middle sections.

pins.name: Toilet – Namcheon end of the beach (수영구 생태 공중화장실)
pins.desc: Suyeong-gu eco toilet near the Namcheon end.

pins.name: Toilet – Millak Waterfront Park (공중화장실)
pins.desc: Public toilet at the waterfront park.

pins.name: Toilet – Millak Waterfront Park, gate side (민락수변공원)
pins.desc: Second public toilet by the park gate.

pins.name: Toilet – Jagalchi quay (자갈치 공중화장실)
pins.desc: Public toilet on Jagalchi-haean-ro, outside the market hall.

pins.name: Toilet – Gukje Market (국제시장)
pins.desc: Toilets inside the market arcades.

pins.name: Toilet – Huinnyeoul village centre (흰여울문화마을거점센터)
pins.desc: Toilets at the village's visitor centre on Jeoryeong-ro.

pins.name: Toilet – Gamcheon Culture Village (감천문화마을공중화장실)
pins.desc: Public toilet in the village.

pins.name: Toilet – Haedong Yonggungsa car park (해동용궁사주차장)
pins.desc: Toilets at the car park by the bus stop.

pins.name: Gwangalli Sikgam – Korean table (광안리 식감)
pins.desc: Popular Korean restaurant a block from the beach. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Haengbok Sikdang – home cooking (광안리 행복식당)
pins.desc: Simple home-style meals behind the beach. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Chaseonchaek – rooftop bridge view café (차선책 본점)
pins.desc: The big rooftop café on the strip, bridge straight ahead; busiest at sunset. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: TTT – bridge view café (티티티)
pins.desc: Upper-floor café facing the bridge; good for the light show. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Esso Café – beachfront (광안리 에쏘카페)
pins.desc: Small café right on the beach road. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: LAF Gwangalli – bakery café (라프 광안리점)
pins.desc: Bakery café on the café street. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Working Holiday – brunch (워킹홀리데이)
pins.desc: Brunch place behind the beach, busy at weekends. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Paldo Tongdak – whole fried chicken (팔도통닭)
pins.desc: Old-style whole fried chicken, the beach chimaek classic. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Outdark Gwangan – chicken and beer (아웃닭 광안점)
pins.desc: Chicken with the bridge view, take-away to the beach. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Gyeongpo Sanghoe – Millak fish market stall (민락회센터 경포상회)
pins.desc: A stall in the Millak fish centre: pick your fish, eat upstairs or in the park. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Oryukdo Hoetjip – raw fish with a bridge view (광안리 전망대 오륙도횟집)
pins.desc: Raw-fish restaurant with the bridge in the window at the Millak end. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Yunhui Hoetjip – raw fish (윤희횟집 광안리본점)
pins.desc: Long-running raw-fish house by the waterfront park. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Yuksomun – Korean beef, Nampo-dong (남포동 육소문)
pins.desc: Beef restaurant in the Nampo-dong lanes. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Chonggak Sanghoe – Jagalchi stall 183 (총각상회 자갈치시장 183호)
pins.desc: Jagalchi market stall with upstairs seating. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Seunggi ssiat hotteok – BIFF Square (승기씨앗호떡)
pins.desc: The seed-stuffed sugar pancake carts of BIFF Square. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Nampo-dong original chapssal hotteok (남포동 원조 찹쌀호떡 본점)
pins.desc: Rice-flour hotteok stall near Gukje Market. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: The Time Now – café, Nampo-dong (더타임나우)
pins.desc: Café in the Gwangbok-ro lanes. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Top Floor – rooftop café, Nampo-dong (탑플로어)
pins.desc: Rooftop café over the Nampo-dong streets. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Huinnyeoul Beach – cliff café (흰여울비치)
pins.desc: Café on the Huinnyeoul cliff lane with the sea below. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Haille – Huinnyeoul café (헤일르)
pins.desc: Sea-view café in the village. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Lisboa – Huinnyeoul café (리스보아)
pins.desc: Portuguese-style café on the cliff lane. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Huinnyeoul Jeomppang – snacks (흰여울점빵)
pins.desc: Village snack shop on the lane. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Asteroid B612 café – Gamcheon (감천문화마을 소행성B612카페)
pins.desc: Café by the Little Prince statue with the village view. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Kkachi Kkachi – Gamcheon café (까치까치 감천문화마을 본점)
pins.desc: Café and dessert shop in the village. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Café Avant-garde – Gamcheon (카페아방가르드)
pins.desc: Rooftop café over the pastel houses. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Mongsil Jongga – pork rice soup, Gamcheon (몽실종가돼지국밥 감천문화마을 본점)
pins.desc: Busan's dwaeji-gukbap at the village entrance. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Sowon-tteul – rest café at Yonggungsa (소원뜰 해동용궁사쉼)
pins.desc: Café at the temple gate. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Dokkaebi Bangatgan – hanok café, Yonggungsa (도깨비방앗간한옥카페 해동용궁사점)
pins.desc: Hanok café on the lane up from the temple. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.

pins.name: Yonggung seafood kalguksu (용궁해물칼국수 기장 오시리아점)
pins.desc: Seafood knife-cut noodles on the coast road near the temple. Still in business on Naver as of 2026-10-22.
